title: Tenant-scoped security-group profiles and automated DNS snapshot rollback
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: Customers running Private installs with multi-tenant host VPCs asked for finer-grained control over control-plane security groups (to separate tenant-to-controlplane egress rules) and safer automated rollbacks of Route53 / resolver changes during upgrades. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) tenant-scoped security-group profiles that let operators attach per-tenant SG templates to controlplane subnets and endpoints (implemented as Terraform module enhancements + Helm values wiring), and (2) an automated DNS snapshot-and-rollback mechanism that captures Route53 private zone state before critical installer changes and can revert on validation failures or manual rollback triggers.

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Terraform: ext/terraform-modules/sg-profiles module: new resource set to create tenant-scoped SGs, profile variables, and mapping table used by the installer. The module exposes a minimal set of attributes (name, tenant_id_tag, egress_rules-json) to keep per-tenant policy declarative.
- Terraform: installer-root/main.tf: wires new sg_profiles module, adds conditional references from subnet attachment and privatelink endpoint modules. Added safe-apply flags for initial rollout.
- Helm: charts/private-installer/templates/controlplane-deploy.yaml: added templated annotation hooks for DNS snapshot and in-chart lifecycle pre-upgrade hook. charts/private-installer/values.schema.json expanded to include sgProfiles and dnsSnapshot.enabled/retention config.
- Installer control-plane operator: cmd/installer/upgrade/hooks.go: introduces dns snapshotter hook (calls aws/route53 helper and stores snapshots in S3 with deterministic keys). Added rollback action that can be triggered automatically when post-upgrade validation fails or manually via installer CLI.
- Utilities: pkg/dns/snapshot.go (stateless snapshot + compare + apply-backup), pkg/sg/templater.go (translate profile to Terraform-friendly JSON blob).
- Tests: integration/terraform/sg_profiles_test.tf (unit tests for mapping), e2e/dns-rollback.yaml (end-to-end scenario exercising upgrade -> forced validation failure -> auto-rollback).

Design decisions and rationale:
- Tenant-scoped SG profiles are implemented as opt-in modules and a lightweight mapping so existing single-tenant installs are unaffected. The mapping allows operators to keep a shared baseline SG and layer tenant-specific overrides.
- DNS snapshot storage uses S3 with server-side encryption and a per-installation prefix. Snapshots are time-stamped; the installer keeps the last N snapshots (configurable) to avoid unbounded storage.
- Rollback semantics: snapshot taken before any Route53 changes; after the upgrade, a validation step runs (DNS checks + controlplane health checks). On validation failure, the snapshotter applies the most recent snapshot and reports detailed diff to the operator. Manual rollback via installer CLI is also supported.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior: sgProfiles disabled, dnsSnapshot.enabled = true (writes snapshots only, does not alter existing DNS unless rollback triggered). Operators can enable tenant-scoped profiles by setting values.sgpProfiles and providing mapping.
- Migration path: included a migration script (scripts/migrate-sg-profiles.sh) to translate legacy inline SG rules into the new profile objects for customers who opt in. Migration is not automatic.
- Safety: terraform changes guarded by a new boolean var safe_apply=true by default; setting safe_apply=false allows more aggressive in-place updates (documented in the README). Helm hook includes a timeout and idempotency checks to avoid blocking upgrades.

Testing and validation:
- CI: Ran terraform plan/apply against the local test account (mocked AWS endpoints) in CI; unit tests for snapshot compare and SG templater added.
- E2E: Added a deterministic scenario: perform upgrade with a broken post-upgrade validator (simulated failure) and verify rollback restores Route53 records and security groups to snapshot state. Test artifact logs attached (links to CI artifact id: ci/installer/882650/artifacts).

Review conversation (abridged, single continuous string):
- Marco Rossi (reviewer): "Can you document how SG precedence is evaluated? I'm worried about accidental open egress rules when mapping overrides don't contain defaults."
- Aisha (author): "Added a precedence section in README and implemented a validation that refuses profile creation without an explicit baseline. Also added an integration test that checks default baseline is applied if missing."
- Diane Park (reviewer): "The DNS rollback looks good. Two small asks: 1) include a dry-run flag for apply-backup, 2) surface S3 encryption config in values."
- Aisha: "Added dry-run mode and exposed s3.kmsKeyId in values.schema. Also tightened IAM policy for snapshotter to least privilege."
- Omar Al-Hassan (approver): "Ran smoke tests in staging and verified rollback scenario. Approving pending CI green. Note: consider perf impact on very large zones (tracked in ENG-4387)."
- CI: initial run failed on lint (helm template warning). Author fixed templates and re-ran; final CI status: pass.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Change log entry appended to CHANGELOG.md under "private-installer" heading with brief usage notes and a link to the migration script.
